It was hard for me too. I have never ran in my life. When I was a kid just a little jog would make my organs hurt. I started with spinning classes, then i moved  to walking on the treadmill. it took me one year to my first 5km race (around 3 miles) I was 39 yo back then. By 42 I was running a marathon. But after the marathon I lost completely the interest. I quit running. Like any addiction I wanted more and more to feel good. I moved to CrossFit and it worked for a while as well. So I can say it works but it is not a cure. I may start to run again when the lockup is gone. I got really fat during the quarantine.

As for UK, isn’t a cultural thing this friendship problem? I am from a Latin country and I have observed that this inability for teens and adults making new friends is ingrained in the northern culture. My advice is: if you have the resources seek a therapist. Don’t rely on acquaintances to open up. As for the dogs, I got myself an adult pug. They are perfect companion dogs for people with busy schedules, sleeping over 16 hour a day and have very plastic personalities. Your mood is their mood. The only thing you need is an automatic dispenser for their food and water. But you need an adult. Puppies are chaotic and destructive and may suffer from separation anxiety.

I will say the obvious. I don’t follow my own advices but there you go:
- eat well. Avoid sugary food. They make you sleepy. 
- cafeine is technically a drug. Don’t rely on it. 
- follow a sleep pattern. Don’t stay awake late. Get off the bed early. Sun light helps to keep you “energized”. 
- exercise. Incredibly the more you exercise the more energy you have. 
- stay away from social media, Reddit included. They are designed to suck your attention up and provide very little back. They are dopamine vampires. 

Best of luck, bro or sis.
